method: Review 35 pending phrases against pages 16–20, keeping narrated statistics, insurance claims and hazardous conduct separate from language instruction. Add targeted expressions for unresolved everyday and structural barriers.
phrases: right off the bat
immediately, from the beginning
一开始就；立刻
Right off the bat, we noticed a problem with the schedule.
一开始我们就注意到日程有问题。
Informal idiom with a baseball image; not literally removing a bat. Source describes an initial assumption, not its accuracy.
turn of events
a development that changes how a situation unfolds
事态的发展或转折
An unexpected turn of events changed our plans.
事态出现意想不到的转折，改变了我们的计划。
Common with unexpected or surprising. Source immediately adds allegedly; the transition does not prove the ensuing account.
fall from heights
an incident in which someone falls from a high place
高处坠落
The safety report discusses injuries caused by falls from heights.
安全报告讨论了高处坠落造成的伤害。
Source's singular fall from heights is a category label; falls from heights is natural for multiple incidents. No prevalence is inferred from the list.
slip and fall
an incident involving losing footing and falling
滑倒事故
The report describes a slip-and-fall accident near the entrance.
报告描述了入口附近的一起滑倒事故。
Use hyphens before a noun in edited prose: slip-and-fall accident. Not automatically proof of anyone's legal responsibility.
the biggest type of
the largest category within a stated comparison
最大的一类……
Support requests were the biggest type of task that week.
那一周，支持请求是数量最多的一类任务。
Biggest may mean number, size or importance; source's ranking context suggests frequency in a described dataset, not severity.
fall off
drop from the surface or edge of something
从……上掉下来
A book fell off the shelf.
一本书从架子上掉了下来。
Fall off of is a common conversational variant in the source. Distinguish fall out of a window from fall off a roof.
it seems to be a thing
it appears to be a recognizable practice or trend
这似乎是一种确实存在的做法或现象
Weekly walking meetings seem to be a thing in some offices.
每周开步行会议，在一些办公室似乎成了一种做法。
Informal a thing means a phenomenon, not a physical object; seems and some do not claim a universal practice.
roll out of
move out of a place by turning or rolling
滚出；翻滚着离开
The ball rolled out of the open bag.
球从敞开的包里滚了出来。
Literal movement here; informal roll out of bed can elsewhere mean get up lazily. Source lists several possible fall situations, not one continuous trajectory.
biggest type of lawsuit
the most prominent or largest category of legal actions in the comparison
占比最大的一类诉讼
The chart identifies the biggest type of lawsuit in its sample.
图表指出了其样本中占比最大的一类诉讼。
Source compares categories in reported data. Biggest does not itself specify frequency versus cost, so the sample and measure must be supplied before making a statistical claim.
in extreme cases
in the most severe or unusual situations
在极端情况下；在最严重的情况下
In extreme cases, the entire system may need to be replaced.
在极端情况下，可能需要更换整个系统。
Limits a statement to severe cases, not the usual outcome. Medical consequences in the source remain reported, not advice.
one would think
a person might reasonably expect
按理说；人们可能会认为
One would think clearer labels would prevent confusion.
按理说，更清楚的标签应该能避免混淆。
Often introduces an expectation challenged by reality. One is generic, and would softens the assertion.
ban Greek life
prohibit the fraternity and sorority system or its activities in the specified setting
禁止校园兄弟会与姐妹会体系或相关活动
The debate asked whether the college should ban Greek life.
辩论讨论了学校是否应该禁止兄弟会与姐妹会体系。
Greek life is campus organizations, not Greek culture generally. Source describes students' advocacy, not an enacted ban.
benefit a lot from
gain substantial help or advantage from something
从……中获益很多
New staff benefit a lot from regular feedback.
新员工从定期反馈中获益很多。
Benefit from + noun or -ing. Source's institutional benefits are the narrator's argument, not quantified proof of net value.
bottom line incentive
a financial motive tied to the final profit or cost outcome
经济利益方面的动机
Reducing waste creates a bottom-line incentive for the business.
减少浪费能给企业带来经济利益方面的动力。
Bottom line is financial outcome, not the literal last line on a page. Hyphenate bottom-line before a noun in edited writing; source spelling is preserved.
built-in marketing
promotion that occurs as an inherent part of an existing arrangement
自带的宣传效应
The visible logo provides built-in marketing for the brand.
醒目的标志为品牌自带宣传效果。
Built-in is metaphorical integration, not necessarily a physical installation. Source analogy does not establish measured advertising value.
don't have to
are not required or do not need to do something
不必；不需要
You don't have to print the document.
你不必打印这份文件。
Absence of necessity, not prohibition: don't have to is different from must not. Source discusses an asserted reduction in building needs.
financially beneficial
helpful in terms of money or finances
在经济上有利的
Sharing equipment can be financially beneficial for a small team.
共享设备对小团队来说可能在经济上更有利。
Financially limits beneficial to money; it does not imply the arrangement is beneficial in every respect.
getting student loans
obtaining money borrowed to pay for education
申请或获得助学贷款
She compared the costs before getting student loans.
她在申请助学贷款之前比较了费用。
Loans are borrowed funds, not scholarships or free money. The sentence is a language example, not a recommendation to borrow.
more enticing to
more attractive or tempting to a particular person
对……更有吸引力
A shorter commute is more enticing to me than a larger office.
比起更大的办公室，更短的通勤对我更有吸引力。
Enticing to + person; than introduces the comparison. Source describes a perceived appeal, not what every student values.
on top of that
in addition to the point already mentioned
除此之外；而且
The room is spacious. On top of that, it's quiet.
房间很宽敞，而且还很安静。
Adds another benefit or problem; not a physical stacking instruction in this discourse use.
one in every eight
one out of each group of eight, as a proportion
每八个中有一个
In this sample, one in every eight responses was incomplete.
在这个样本中，每八份回复就有一份不完整。
Equivalent proportion to one in eight; not every eighth person in a literal sequence. Source attributes the housing figure to some colleges, not all institutions.
the promise of
the appealing prospect or expectation of something
……的诱人前景；……的期待
The promise of more free time made the shorter commute appealing.
能有更多空闲时间的前景，让更短的通勤显得很有吸引力。
Here an appealing prospect, not necessarily a binding spoken promise. The source's risky example is not reproduced as an instruction.
they don't have to
the people or organizations mentioned do not need to do something
他们或它们不必……
They don't have to attend every session.
他们不必参加每一场活动。
They requires a clear antecedent; in source it resumes universities after a spoken topic shift. Not a ban on attendance or construction.
according to
as stated or reported by a specified source
根据……所述
According to the report, attendance increased.
根据报告，出席人数增加了。
Attributes information rather than proving it. The source has awkward one research wording; use one study in neutral teaching prose without changing the quote.
at least according to
limiting a claim to what a named source reports
至少根据……的说法
The project is on schedule, at least according to the latest update.
项目按计划进行，至少最新进展说明是这么说的。
At least restricts the basis for the statement rather than counting sources. A single report is not independent confirmation.
burns down
is destroyed or severely damaged by fire
被烧毁
The novel begins after the old house burns down.
小说从那座老房子被烧毁后开始。
Intransitive burn down describes destruction; burn a building down is transitive. The fictional teaching example does not describe a podcast event.
by bed and by student
calculated per bed and per student in the speaker's description
按床位、按学生人数计算
The hypothetical budget is broken down by bed and by student.
这份假设预算按床位和学生人数分别列出。
By signals the unit or basis of calculation; source's claim about insurance pricing is not verified as a universal method.
expand the number
increase how many there are
增加数量
The team plans to expand the number of available sessions.
团队计划增加可参加的场次。
Expand the number of + plural noun; increase the number is also natural. Source discusses admissions capacity as an argued consequence.
if not the oldest
possibly even the oldest, after asserting membership among the oldest
甚至可能是最古老的
It is one of the oldest buildings here, if not the oldest.
它是这里最古老的建筑之一，甚至可能是最古老的。
Rhetorical strengthening with uncertainty, not the ordinary if something is not condition. Do not turn the source's hedge into a verified historical superlative.
merged into one
combined separate entities into a single entity
合并成一个
The three folders were merged into one.
三个文件夹被合并成了一个。
Merge into emphasizes the resulting single entity; source begins apparently, preserving uncertainty about the historical account.
on campus
within the university's grounds or campus setting
在校园里
She works on campus three days a week.
她每周有三天在校园里工作。
Usually no article in on campus. Source asks about retaining organizations there, rather than stating that a ban occurred.
seem more financially generous
appear more willing to give money
似乎在金钱捐助方面更慷慨
In the survey, returning donors seem more financially generous than first-time donors.
在这项调查中，重复捐助者似乎比首次捐助者在捐款方面更慷慨。
Seem is an evidentiary hedge and more requires a comparison; financial generosity does not describe kindness in all domains.
slip on
lose footing because of a surface or substance
踩到……而滑倒或打滑
He slipped on a wet tile.
他踩到湿瓷砖滑了一下。
Slipping because of a surface here, not slip on a jacket meaning put it on quickly. The presence of water does not itself settle liability.
worth it
valuable enough to justify the effort, cost or risk
值得；值得付出这些代价
The journey was tiring, but it was worth it.
旅途很累，但值得。
It refers to the implied cost or effort. Source asks a value question and uses profanity for emphasis, not as part of the core phrase.
part of Greek life
involved in the fraternity and sorority system
属于或参与校园兄弟会与姐妹会体系
She was part of Greek life while at college.
她上大学时参加了校园姐妹会体系的活动。
Institutional participation, not Greek nationality or language study. Source's donation comparison does not prove causation.
tied with
equal in rank or score to another item
与……并列
The team was tied with its rival for fifth place.
这支队伍与对手并列第五。
Tied is equal rank here, not physically bound. Source's tied with fifth is compressed speech for sharing fifth place.
auto accidents
accidents involving motor vehicles
机动车事故；车祸
The report lists auto accidents as a separate category.
报告把机动车事故列为单独一类。
Auto is an American shortening of automobile, not automatic. Source's percentage belongs to the cited comparison, not a general rate for all students.
the light side
the supposedly less serious end of a range in this context
相对较轻的一面（这里是说话者的归类）
The review treats the delay as the light side of the project's problems.
这份评估把延期视为项目问题中相对较轻的一面。
Not illumination or automatically a humorous side. Source minimizes some harmful conduct relative to worse acts; the wording does not make that conduct safe or acceptable.
full-on
complete, intense or outright, informally
彻底的；十足的；全面的
A small disagreement became a full-on argument.
一个小分歧变成了一场激烈争吵。
Informal intensifier before a noun or adjective. In source it contrasts a purportedly lighter category with outright sexual assault; not a safety distinction.
a bunk bed
a bed arrangement with one bed above another
一张上下铺床
The small room has a bunk bed and a desk.
这个小房间里有一张上下铺床和一张书桌。
Compound names stacked sleeping spaces. Source lists separate dangerous fall situations; do not infer a single uninterrupted sequence.
puddle of water
a small shallow pool of water on a surface
一小摊积水
There was a puddle of water near the doorway.
门口附近有一小摊积水。
Puddle is small and shallow, not a pond. The source says might sue, which is a possible legal action rather than established liability.
segments: Fall category, vehicle accidents and equal ranking are explicitly taught. Seven percent is retained as the narrator's sample-based figure, not a universal rate; ranked items are not confused with physical tying.
Figurative lesser-severity meaning and the narrator's minimizing comparison are explicit; covered means understandable, not harmless or endorsed.
The repeated comparison now links to the same contextual warning that supposedly less severe harm remains harmful.
Full-on is taught as outright/intense, and side means an aspect of the practice; the linked assault vocabulary explains the harm without adding instructions or case findings.

Bunk-bed compound and rolling movement are now explicit alongside the escape card's fire-escape sense and the balcony definition. The disfluent list gives several fall locations rather than one person falling through every location in sequence.
Organization types and the proportional expression are all explained. Some colleges limits the narrator's statistic, and lives agrees with one.
The slippery-surface sense and shallow-pool noun are taught; might sue indicates possible action, not automatic legal responsibility.
